1.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [gained complete control over his kingdom] or [ruled powerfully over his kingdom]
This is the name of God that he revealed to his people in the Old Testament. See the translationWord page about Yahweh concerning how to translate this.
Here “was with him” is an idiom. Alternate translation: [God supported him] or [God helped him]

2.note:
# General Information:

It may be helpful to reorder the events in these verses as in the UST.

2.q: spoke to all Israel, to the commanders … heads of the fathers’ house
2.note: Here “all of Israel” means those people mentioned afterwards. They represent all of Israel. Alternate translation: [spoke to the commanders … heads of the father’s house]

2.q: the commanders of thousands and of hundreds
2.note: This could mean: (1) these numbers represent the exact amount of soldiers that these commanders led. Alternate translation: [the commanders of 1,000 soldiers and the commanders of 100 soldiers] or (2) the words translated as [thousands] and “hundreds” do not represent exact numbers, but are the names of larger and smaller military divisions. Alternate translation: [the commanders of large military divisions and the commanders of smaller military divisions]

2.q: to every prince in all Israel, the heads of the fathers’ houses
2.note: Here “the heads of the fathers’ houses” further describe the princes. Alternate translation: [to every prince in all Israel, that is, the heads of the fathers’ houses]
Here “prince” means leaders in general. They are not necessarily the sons of the king. Alternate translation: [to every leader]

2.q: the heads of the fathers’ houses
2.note: Here “heads” is a metaphor for the most important part. And “houses” represents families. Alternate translation: [the leaders of the families in Israel] (See also: [Metonymy](ta:figs-metonymy))

4.note: A little town about 9 miles west of Jerusalem.

5.q: the bronze altar made by Bezalel son of Uri son of Hur
5.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri son Hur made]

5.q: Bezalel son of Uri son of Hur

6.note: Alternate translation: [went up to the high place at Gibeon]

7.q: Ask! What should I give you?
7.note: If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [Ask for whatever you want from me.]

8.q: You have shown great covenant faithfulness to David
8.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you can express the same idea with a verbal form such as “faithfully” or “faithful.” Alternate translation: [You have greatly and faithfully loved David] or [You have been very faithful to David]

9.note: Here the word “Now” is used to draw attention to the important point that follows.

9.q: let your promise to David my father be carried out
9.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [please do what you promised to David my father that you would do]

9.q: a people as numerous as the dust of the earth
9.note: This simile emphasizes the great number of Israelites. Alternate translation: [countless people] or [very many people]

10.note: This can be restated to remove the abstract nouns “wisdom” and “knowledge.” Alternate translation: [cause me to be wise and to know many things]

10.q: who can judge your people, who are so many in number?
10.note: Here “judge” means to govern or rule. Solomon uses a question to state that it is impossible to rule over so many people without God’s help. Alternate translation: [no one can judge all of your countless people without your help.]

11.q: Because this was in your heart
11.note: Here “heart” represents desire. Alternate translation: [Because this was your desire] or [Because this is what you wanted]

11.q: nor for the life of those who hate you
11.note: Alternate translation: [nor to be able to defeat those who hate you] or [nor to be able to kill your enemies]

12.q: I will now give you wisdom and knowledge
12.note: This can be restated to remove the abstract nouns “wisdom” and “knowledge.” Alternate translation: [I will now cause you to be wise and to know many things]

13.note: Here “Solomon” represents all the people with him. Also “came” can be stated as “went.” Alternate translation: [So Solomon and the people with him went to Jerusalem] (See also: [Go and Come](ta:figs-go))

13.q: from before the tent of meeting
13.note: Alternate translation: [from the tent of meeting]

14.note: This is a reference to cities which stored his chariots.

15.q: The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as the stones
15.note: The narrator uses exaggeration to emphasize the great amount of silver that was in Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [The king had so much silver in Jerusalem, it was like there was as much silver as there was stones on the ground]
This is a tree that grows fruit that looks like figs.

16.q: As for the importation of horses from Egypt and Kue for Solomon
16.note: “Importation” is the act of bringing something into one country from another country. This can be stated as a verb. Alternate translation: [As for the horses Solomon imported from Egypt and Kue]
This is the name of a region. Some think that Kue was the same as Cilicia, in Asia Minor.
Alternate translation: [at a set price] or [for money]

17.q: six hundred shekels of silver & 150 shekels
17.note: A shekel is a unit of weight equal to about 11 grams. Alternate translation: [about 6.6 kilograms of silver … about 1.7 kilograms]
to send something out of one country into another
